podcast.title: Development and Opening Slots
podcast.body: Mighty Joe Young spent about two years playing numerous gigs to develop their sound and performance skills, eventually drawing audiences of a couple hundred people on their own. This success led to opening slots for bands such as Solar Sylem and the Rollins Band. "This band worked out their chops by playing gig after gig for about two years, eventually drawing a couple hundred people on their own which led to opening slots for bands like Solar Sylem and the Rollins band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Gig
podcast.body: The band's inaugural performance took place in August 1990 at The Whiskey on Sunset Boulevard in Los Angeles. "The first gig was in August of 1990 at the whiskey on Sunset Boulevard in Los Angeles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Forced Name Change
podcast.body: The band was compelled to change their name from Mighty Joe Young because an old Chicago blues singer, also named Joe Young, objected to their use of the name. This happened just two days before they were scheduled to submit their debut album to Atlantic Records. "An old Chicago blues singer named Joe Young, objected to the band using the name Mighty Joe Young because that's the name he used to use."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence of Red Hot Chili Peppers
podcast.body: During the late 1980s, when hair metal was popular and grunge was still emerging, Robert DeLeo, a big fan of Flea and the Red Hot Chili Peppers' funkiness, influenced Mighty Joe Young's sound, as evident in some of their early songs like "Dirty Dog." "Robert Delayo was a big fan of flea in the funkiness of the Red Hot Chili Peppers who were finally starting to do well."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Original Name of Stone Temple Pilots
podcast.body: The band that would become Stone Temple Pilots initially formed in San Diego under the name Muddy Joe Young. "They first came together in San Diego under the name Muddy Joe Young."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Groups That Changed Their Front-Person and Survived

podcast.title: San Diego Misconception
podcast.body: The band got a bunch of gigs in San Diego, partly due to Dean DeLeo's help, which led to the misconception that Stone Temple Pilots originated from San Diego. "Dean Delayo wasn't much interested in being in a band at all, but he did help his brother and Scott and Eric get a bunch of gigs in San Diego, which is where the misconception of STP being a San Diego band started."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: First Gig Location and Date
xref.body: As Mighty Joe Young, the band played their first ever gig in August 1990 at The Whiskey on Sunset Boulevard in Los Angeles. "The first gig was in August of 1990 at the whiskey on Sunset Boulevard in Los Angeles."

xref.title: Influence on Mighty Joe Young
xref.body: Robert DeLeo of Mighty Joe Young (later Stone Temple Pilots) was a significant fan of Flea and the Red Hot Chili Peppers' funkiness. This influence was noticeable in Mighty Joe Young's sound, particularly in early demos like "Dirty Dog," during a period when hair metal was big and grunge was still years away. "Robert Delayo was a big fan of flea in the funkiness of the Red Hot Chili Peppers who were finally starting to do well."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Name Change Due to Legal Dispute
xref.body: Just two days before delivering their debut album to Atlantic Records, the band was informed by their lawyer that they had a problem: an old Chicago blues singer named Joe Young objected to them using the name Mighty Joe Young. This forced the group to find a new name within two weeks. "An old Chicago blues singer named Joe Young, objected to the band using the name Mighty Joe Young because that's the name he used to use."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Original Name: Mighty Joe Young
xref.body: Before becoming Stone Temple Pilots, the group was known as Mighty Joe Young, named after a character in a 1940s gorilla movie. They performed their first gig under this name. "At this point, the group was known as Mighty Joe Young after the character in that gorilla movie from the 1940s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Record Deal with Atlantic Records
xref.body: An agent who saw the band play tipped off Atlantic Records, who observed the group multiple times. Following a show at The Shamrock in Silver Lake, an offer was made, and Mighty Joe Young signed their major label deal on April 1st, 1992 (April Fool's Day). "And on April 1st 1992, April Fool's Day, Mighty Joe Young signed their major label deal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Sound Development and Influences
xref.body: For about two years, the band worked on their sound by playing numerous gigs, developing their chops. In the late 1980s, hair metal was prevalent, and grunge was yet to fully emerge. Robert DeLeo's admiration for Flea and the funkiness of Red Hot Chili Peppers significantly influenced their early sound, particularly as Mighty Joe Young. "Took a while to figure out their sound too."
